verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is expected to land around 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '5:07 p.m. PDT on April 10'; R2: 'around 8:07 p.m. (5:07 p.m. PDT) Friday, April 10'; R3: 'around 8:07 p.m. ET'; R5: 'about 8:07 p.m. ET'; R6: 'around 5:07 p.m. PT'; R7: 'around 20:00 Friday US EDT'; R8: 'around 8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple references explicitly state the time in PDT/EDT (equivalent to ET), matching precisely with correct conversion.

verifications.claim: The recovery vessel for the Artemis II landing is the USS John P. Murtha.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'flown to the USS John P. Murtha... transport them to the USS Murtha'; R3: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel... USS John P. Murtha'; R4: 'recovery ship USS John P. Murtha'; R6: 'U.S. Navy recovery vessel... USS John P. Murtha'; R7: 'USS John P. Murtha that will bring them home'
verifications.reasoning: Several references directly name the USS John P. Murtha as the recovery vessel/ship for the crew post-splashdown.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II capsule will use a parachute-assisted landing to reach the ocean surface at approximately 17 mph.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'slow down to roughly 17 mph when it lands in the ocean, thanks to the deployment of several parachutes'; R2: 'deploy its drogue parachutes... three main parachutes... for splashdown'; R3: 'parachute-assisted splashdown... slow Orion from about 130 mph to just 17 mph'; R5: 'parachute-assisted water landing'; R6: 'parachute-assisted landing... slow Orion from about 130 mph to just 17 mph'
verifications.reasoning: References directly describe parachute deployment slowing the capsule to ~17 mph for ocean splashdown.
